ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004), as amended by the Law of 1 February 2024 and the Law of 29 July 2024 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849, Directive (EU) 2018/843, Directive (EU) 2018/1673 and applying Regulation (EU) 2024/1624; Loi modifiée du 13 janvier 2019 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE Law of 13 January 2019), as amended by the Law of 10 July 2020; Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés (Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS); Loi modifiée du 31 mai 1999 sur la domiciliation des sociétés (Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation); CSSF Règlement 20-03 of 20 January 2020 on AML/CFT professional obligations and supervision; Loi modifiée du 11 janvier 2008 relative aux mesures de gel des avoirs et d'interdiction de mise à disposition de fonds (asset-freezing sanctions law).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for non-EU/EEA documents) or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague-Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement, maximum three months old)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization only where the Luxembourg notary does not accept uncertified bank statements; generally no apostille required for EU/EEA bank statements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and registry extract of each corporate shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (mandatory when the corporate shareholder is registered outside the EU/EEA)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of each corporate shareholder or corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax administration of the shareholder's country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required by the notary and the account-holding Luxembourg credit institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter forming part of the source-of-funds declaration for the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Custodian bank or financial institution of the funding party

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signature screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers and directors against the CSSF consolidated PEP register, the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) 833/2014, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the Luxembourg asset-freezing list under the Law of 11 January 2008, FATF high-risk jurisdiction advisories and, given the target payment rails with Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the United States OFAC SDN list; a documented negative screening report is required by the Luxembourg notary and the account-holding credit institution, with enhanced due diligence triggered by any PEP match, high-risk third-country residence, adverse media, or unexplained source-of-funds anomaly.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — official portal www.lbr.lu (RCS: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin characters; French is the customary official language of the articles of association, with Luxembourgish and German also accepted; any non-Latin commercial name (e.g., CJK or Cyrillic) must be transliterated into a Latin-character version for RCS registration and publication in RESA; the legal name of an SARL must contain the suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.' and must be distinct from all existing RCS entries and not misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a requested corporate name by the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS via LBR), the applicant must file a formal written request for reconsideration (recours gracieux) with the RCS department of the LBR within ten (10) working days of the decision, attaching the original name-reservation receipt, the draft articles of association, and evidence of the planned RESA publication; if the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may lodge an annulment appeal (recours en annulation) before the Tribunal Administratif of Luxembourg within three (3) months of the refusal decision, asserting legal error, misapplication of Article 17-1 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, or breach of distinctiveness assessment principles; to preserve the incorporation timetable, an alternative name should be reserved during the appeal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are administratively permissible as the initial registered-office address (siège social) of an SARL, provided the domiciliation provider holds ministerial approval under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies; however, for a digital health fitness app tracker enterprise classified under ISIC 6201 with recurring cross-border payment rails through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, a virtual office without genuine local management, payroll substance, and physical records materially elevates the risk of denial of treaty benefits and tax substance audit; the Administration des Contributions Directes applies Article 14 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) and the OECD anti-BEPS substance doctrine, and the incorporation notary will verify the intended administrative seat (siège administratif) and may decline formalisation where the seat is purely fictitious.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate quantified likelihood of 30%–35% of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months after RCS registration, reflecting (i) CSSF AML/CFT inspections of licensed domiciliation providers, (ii) corporate-tax substance audits targeting digitally active SARLs with no local employees and offshore controllers, and (iii) LBR/RBE beneficial-ownership verification exercises; the likelihood is partially mitigated by the low-risk AML classification of the fitness app product line but heightened by reliance on platform payment rails and Apple/Google processing data.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (custodian bank holding the capital in escrow)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 for an SARL pursuant to the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as modified by the Law of 23 December 2016; converted at 1 EUR = 1.08 USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarisation of the articles of association (acte constitutif and statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff scale under the Loi du 13 décembre 1989 on judicial and notarial fees, market benchmark EUR 1,500–3,500 per standard SARL incorporation, average EUR 3,500 including drafts and effective 1 EUR = 1.08 USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation registration fee (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR registry tariff of EUR 150 per incorporation filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RESA mandatory publication of the incorporation deed in the electronic gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RESA publication service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RESA electronic-gazette publication fee of EUR 50 per company act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and availability reservation via LBR portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal statutory or administrative LBR fee of EUR 50 for certified name-availability verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee applicable; UBO declaration must be filed within one (1) month of RCS registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company or corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 1,200–2,000 per annum for approved domiciliation, mail handling and substance-file preparation, average EUR 1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-border legal counsel fees (pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing, shareholder documentation, AML/KYC kit)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark partner hourly rates of EUR 350–600 for six to ten hours, or fixed fee of EUR 3,500–4,500 for a standard SARL incorporation with a clean UBO chain

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille and consular legalisation of foreign UBO identity, corporate and source-of-funds documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening, KYC and counterparty due-diligence fee for the SARL operating account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution holding the corporate account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 300–500 one-time account-opening and due-diligence verification fee, average USD 500

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (in particular Articles 710-1 to 710-22 governing the SARL), and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), managed by the Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés) filed with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000; fully subscribed and paid up in cash before incorporation, deposited in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution or bank
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers adopt the articles of association of the Company and allocate the share capital of EUR 12,000 to the initial shareholders, such capital being fully subscribed and paid into the Company's escrow bank account. RESOLVED that the Company's registered office be established at [address in Luxembourg] and the board of managers is authorized to execute the lease and file the address with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed as Manager (Gérant) with authority to represent the Company, and [Name] be appointed as Compliance Officer responsible for corporate filings. All actions to complete incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and Register the Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) / e-Application via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative certificate search through the RCS electronic portal to ensure availability of the proposed corporate name. Submit the name reservation request, attach proof of identity of the founding shareholder(s), and pay the applicable search fee. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 2 months, renewable for a further 2 months upon request.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of founding shareholders and managers
Power of attorney (if a professional filer is engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried, amend the suffix and resubmit by completing a revised name reservation request; objections require a formal reply to the RCS with a justification of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Blocked Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Luxembourg bank (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Luxembourg, or a credit institution authorized by the CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Contact the bank and submit the pre-incorporation file including the draft notarial deed and proof of name reservation. The bank opens a blocked escrow account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 in cash, obtain a debit confirmation (attestation de blocage) to be delivered to the notary.
required_dossiers: Identification documents and economic residence proof of beneficial owners
Bank KYC forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening, remedy by providing enhanced corporate documents or selecting an alternative licensed bank and resubmitting the KYC package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the final articles of association, bank blocked-funds certificate, and identity documentation of managers and shareholders. The notary drafts the notarial deed, verifies legal capacity and capital. The deed is signed in person or by proxy before the notary, authenticating the incorporation effective as of that date.
required_dossiers: Identification documents and residential addresses of founders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query, correct the capital allocation or legal capacity documentation and re-execute the deed; the notary may also require additional declarations on beneficial ownership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via the e-filing platform of guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarial signature, the notary or company representative files the authentic deed, coordinated articles, and identification documents electronically. The RCS examines the compliance and registers the company under a unique business number (numéro d'immatriculation). The filing fees are settled online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the file, remedy by submitting supplementary declarations, legalizing translations, or paying the remaining fee; requests for correction must be filed within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Statutory Notice and Register for Corporate Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – centralized publication; Administration des Contributions Directes; Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS publishes the incorporation details in the electronic compendium of companies (Recueil électronique des sociétés, RESA). Simultaneously, the company is automatically registered with the tax authorities. Thereafter, register for social security with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale and obtain an employer number. Verify the date of effective existence for VAT registration if deemed necessary by the business plan.
required_dossiers: Tax and social security registration forms
ID documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, contact the RCS to accelerate the release; social security registration queries are resolved by supplementation of the registration application with statutory details.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing activity; for digital health software, no industrial license is required under the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 – Exempt (office-based digital activity with no industrial or physical installation)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater or VOC discharge. General requirement to manage electronic waste (WEEE) and packaging waste (ELV) in accordance with Luxembourg environmental regulations. Any office lease must comply with sanitary standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local commune and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) approval are required only for physical premises. For this digital activity, only standard occupational health and safety compliance for office workspaces is recommended, including rescue plan and workplace Ergo/GVH assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Luxembourg VAT and indirect tax administration, portal: https://aedt.gouvernement.lu, business e-filing portal: https://guichet.lu. Direct corporate tax administration: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu. Company registry and matricule issuance: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), portal: https://www.lbr.lu.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); FX control and treasury-related compliance oversight is also exercised by the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for anti-money laundering, sanctions, and payment services supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg does not operate an exchange control system. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account by virtue of Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the 1999 Law on the Monetary Status of the Euro, and the CSSF/BCL regulatory framework. Dividends, distributions, loan repayments, and capital repatriation are payable without prior FX authorization. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate law formalities and withholding tax administration rather than currency convertibility constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no prescribed repatriation deadlines for export receipts in Luxembourg. A Luxembourg SARL may retain export proceeds in foreign currency accounts or convert them freely. Periodic balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations apply to resident entities under ECB Regulation ECB/2013/31, but they do not restrict timing, conversion, or disposition.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium for EU-licensed fintech EMI solutions and Low for offshore digital EMIs outside the EEA. Luxembourg permits the use of CSSF-licensed electronic money institutions and EU/EEA EMIs passporting under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2). An offshore EMI without an EU passport cannot lawfully maintain an operational payment account for a Luxembourg SARL. Even with a compliant EMI, the SARL may still require a credit institution account to meet capital escrow and substance requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a statutory rule requiring all founders to appear physically before a bank; however, in practice, tier-one Luxembourg banks require at least one manager with sole or joint signature authority to attend an in-person interview. Where directors are non-EU residents, a physical onboarding meeting in Luxembourg or at a notable foreign branch is typically required. Remote video identification may be accepted at bank discretion only after enhanced KYC review and confirmation of the entity's economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owners with complex multi-tier shareholding and no previous Luxembourg banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised certificate of incumbency, LEI certificate, full ownership chain chart, international extract from the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, passport copies, three years of personal bank statements, source of wealth memorandum, and a written corporate summary explaining the SARL's product, market, and Luxembourg substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Initial capital contribution appearing as a third-party deposit or intra-group loan rather than pure equity injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg notary deed of incorporation, bank proof of immediate share capital release, shareholder subscription resolutions, evidence of no fungible mixed funds, and sworn statements that the capital was credited solely from the shareholder's own regulated bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Cross-border IP licensing and digital service fees creating ambiguity about the entity's commercial reality and compliance with anti-money laundering substance checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the registered office lease with a minimum current term exceeding twelve months, employment contracts and Luxembourg social security declarations for local personnel, annual board minutes held in Luxembourg, technical service or royalty agreements in draft, and CSSF bank confirmation from a foreign referent institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Potential politically exposed person (PEP) or central sanctions-list screening result among shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP declaration, legal explanation of the PEP relationship, independent transactional source-of-funds report, regulatory compliance certificate from the home jurisdiction, and a Luxembourg corporate law opinion confirming the legitimacy of the mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital routing should be executed via a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer to the SARL's Luxembourg IBAN using the BoP statistical purpose code for direct investment equity capital, with the reference

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) — balance sheet, profit and loss account and notes, as approved by the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing through MyGuichet (eCDF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date (by 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end); the approving AGM must be held within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 150 imposed by the RCS for late or omitted filing; after a formal reminder and continued default, the tribunal de commerce may order ex officio strike-off of the RCS registration and commencement of liquidation proceedings; directors may incur criminal fines for deliberate non-publication.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register annual confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); e-filing via MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 January, confirming UBO data in force as at 31 December of the preceding year; any UBO change (including a share transfer) must additionally be declared within 1 month of the corresponding event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 250–EUR 1,250 per violation; intentional false or incomplete declarations are criminally sanctioned by imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years and/or a fine of up to EUR 125,000; the company may further be ordered by a court to suspend the voting rights attached to the non-disclosed shareholding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting (AGM) minutes — approval of the annual accounts, discharge of the gérant, profit appropriation and, where applicable, appointment of the réviseur d'entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulatory filing authority — minutes are retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office; notarial form is required only where a shareholder resolution also amends the articles of association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative fine, but each shareholder may petition the tribunal de commerce to convene the meeting at the company's expense; persistent failure constitutes management negligence by the gérant and materially supports administrative strike-off proceedings in conjunction with non-filing of annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate direct tax return — corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IF), filed on Form 400
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Bureau d'imposition having jurisdiction; e-filing through MyGuichet (eCDF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paper filing: by 31 December of the calendar year following the tax year (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 December 2025); electronic filing automatically extends the deadline to 31 May of year N+2 (e.g., 31 May 2026)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax; monthly default interest of 0.91% (approximately 10.92% per annum) on delayed payments; persistent failure enables ex officio taxation with the same surcharge and, in cases of fraudulent omission, a criminal fine of up to EUR 125,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent Luxembourg audit by an accredited réviseur d'entreprises is compulsory when, on two consecutive balance-sheet dates, the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: (i) total balance sheet of EUR 4.4 million; (ii) net turnover of EUR 8.8 million; (iii) annual average workforce of 50 full-time equivalents. Exemption also lapses if consolidated accounts are required or the articles of association mandate a statutory auditor. A small SARL below these thresholds may voluntarily appoint a certified accountant (comptable agréé) for a review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: LUX GAAP as codified by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual and consolidated accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted only for statutory consolidated accounts, while SARL single-entity statutory accounts must follow LUX GAAP; annual accounts comprise a balance sheet, profit and loss account and notes, filed electronically in RCS eCDF/XBRL format.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE must be reconfirmed electronically every January (deadline 31 January) against the situation as at 31 December. Any direct or indirect beneficial owner with an interest exceeding 25% must be identified, documented and filed. A share transfer within an SARL is perfected by a written transfer deed, recorded in the Register of Members (effective against the company), and the resulting UBO chain must be re-filed to the RBE within 1 month of the transfer, before the next annual confirmation cycle. The gérant must collect identity evidence and recalculate the 25% control threshold for each change in the shareholding or control chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book — minutes of general meetings (Procès-verbaux des assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200–US$3,800 per year (EUR 1,100–EUR 3,500) for a Luxembourg registered-office or domiciliation agreement with a licensed fiduciary or regulated professional (PFS), excluding director services, bookkeeping and tax filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required at current SME thresholds; if the EUR 4.4m / EUR 8.8m / 50-employee thresholds are triggered, a Luxembourg statutory audit by a réviseur d'entreprises typically costs US$8,500–US$27,000 (EUR 8,000–EUR 25,000) depending on transaction volume and consolidation scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City fiscal year 2024: national corporate income tax 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT + municipal business tax 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box concession: 80% exemption for qualifying software/patent income, reducing the combined top rate to approximately 4.99% on IP-related profits subject to the OECD nexus ratio; R&D super-deduction of 20% on eligible research staff costs; Notional Interest Deduction on new cash equity (annual Grand-Ducal rate, approx. 1.5-2%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains from a 10%+ shareholding held for at least 12 months; no statutorily fixed tax holiday is available

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return - Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via the eTVA portal on MyGuichet.lu; the annual financial statements must be attached in iXBRL format
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the Luxembourg tax year corresponds to the financial year, ordinarily the calendar year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; an extension to 31 December is available on prior application; quarterly CIT prepayments fall due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered trade name, RCS Luxembourg number, VAT number, legal form, registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not indicated on the form; the SARL files in its own name and must show the local establishment address and the Luxembourg tax office of competence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar-year filing is standard; a different closing date may apply if provided in the articles of association and consistently used

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NACE Rev.2 code 62.01 for computer programming activities; description of the digital health and fitness telemetry application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The description must make clear that the SARL is the developer and operator of the app, receiving Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds as gross business revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets, share capital, legal reserve, net equity, bank debts and other liabilities at the year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance sheet must be prepared under the Luxembourg chart of accounts in EUR and reconciled with the filed annual accounts; no consolidation in the SARL's separate return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross subscription and licence revenue from the app, less Apple/Google commissions, chargebacks and refunds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: App store commissions (15-30%) must be deducted against supporting statements from Apple and Google; transfer-pricing documentation must substantiate that the operating margin is at arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Personnel, cloud infrastructure, marketing, software licences, legal and accounting fees, director fees and depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany invoices must be supported by written contracts and reflect actual economic benefit to the SARL; intra-group charges without substance are disallowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, bank charges, interest on shareholder loans, foreign exchange differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign shareholders must respect the arm's length rate and the thin-capitalisation practice; the Luxembourg debtor must not be required to withhold on interest, subject to substance review

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible taxes, excessive or undocumented remuneration, fines, certain 50% entertainment costs, and depreciation recapture
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors' fees paid in kind or to foreign connected persons may be recharacterised if no board minute or written mandate exists; the tax administration requests substantiation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividend income and capital gains under the participation exemption; 80% of qualifying IP-box income as defined in Article 50bis LIR; non-taxable capital contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach schedules evidencing the 10% shareholding/12-month holding period for the participation exemption and the OECD-compliant nexus calculation for the IP box on software assets of the fitness app

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unrelieved prior-year losses utilised against the current year's taxable basis; maximum period of utilisation is 17 years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss-history reconciliation must be included in the return working papers; a change of control does not automatically forfeit losses in Luxembourg but an anti-abuse review applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments, application of the 17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, municipal business tax of the commune of the principal establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The effective combined headline charge is 24.94% in Luxembourg City; municipal coefficients differ per commune and are applied on the municipal business base

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly CIT prepayments, foreign tax credits, other withholding credits and the final balance due or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: European convention or DTA relief on app-store platform fees is rare; any foreign withholding on income must be proven by foreign tax certificates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the authorised manager (gérant) or the appointed Luxembourg tax representative; declaration of completeness and accuracy
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Out-of-country signatures are acceptable, but the responsible Luxembourg representative must be identified with authority to receive the assessment notice

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 under §167 Abgabenordnung (AO); surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax where filing is delayed beyond 30 days; late-payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum) from the statutory due date; deliberate false filing is tax fraud under §396 AO and carries a fine of up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment of one to five years, and publication of the conviction; the responsible manager may be held personally liable for the penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2003 (Net Wealth Tax Return - Déclaration pour l'impôt sur la fortune) filed simultaneously with Form 1001 via eTVA/MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end, extension to 31 December as for Form 1001

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance-sheet total of the SARL, including cash, receivables, development intangibles and financial participations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All assets worldwide are subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax because the SARL is tax-resident; app-related intangible assets must be recognised at historical cost

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying participations exempted from net wealth tax and deductible liabilities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 100% participation exemption applies; intellectual property used for the app is not exempt and forms part of the net wealth tax base

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth after the EUR 500,000 exemption threshold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable base may be reduced by the relief available for new risk capital subscribed and paid after 17 June 2014

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D - Minimum net wealth tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Minimum net wealth tax determinant based on the balance-sheet total (ranging from EUR 535 to EUR 3,210 for most SMEs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The minimum tax is computed on total assets irrespective of losses; banking secrecy waivers are required for bank confirmations of the balance-sheet total

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E - Net wealth tax charge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 0.5% of taxable net wealth exceeding EUR 500,000 after use of the minimum tax credit mechanism
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The net wealth tax is deductible for corporate income tax purposes only in the year of payment under the standard Luxembourg rule

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same §167 AO fine framework and 0.8% monthly interest regime as Form 1001; under declaring balance-sheet assets in the net wealth tax return constitutes tax evasion with penalties up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to five years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (WHT) on distributions to non-resident shareholders; 0% for qualifying European parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds 10% for 12 months and both companies satisfy the anti-abuse substance requirement
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief, the foreign shareholder must transmit to the Luxembourg paying entity a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its tax residence jurisdiction, together with a completed Form 22 (request for application of the double tax treaty rate or for refund of WHT already withheld); the holding period and 10% threshold are evidenced by share register excerpts and articles of association; for EU/EEA corporate shareholders, a sworn statement that the company is subject to a corporate income tax comparable to Luxembourg CIT and is not exempt must be appended; the Luxembourg administration issues the assessment on WHT, and refund applications must be filed within five years; for the Parent-Subsidiary Directive route the exemption may be applied at source only after prior approval through the concession procedure; failure to file the request in time triggers the full 15% WHT which can still be recuperated via refund or foreign tax credit
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident companies under current LIR Article 149, so cross-border interest flows are generally paid gross; Royalties: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax on royalty payments for intellectual property (including app software licences) paid to non-resident licensees; treaty rates are therefore not operational for interest and royalties; the only residual risk is profit participation loans and certain hybrid instruments which may be recharacterised as dividends subject to 15% WHT

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the Luxembourg entity's net annual turnover equals or exceeds EUR 50,000,000 and cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 in the case of financing transactions or EUR 1,000,000 for other transactions; Master File is mandatory where the consolidated worldwide group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000; below these thresholds the SARL must still keep simplified contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation proportionate to the transactions, including app-store commission arrangements, intercompany service agreements, and IP licensing contracts
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the economic substance doctrine through the general anti-abuse clause (abus de droit) in §6 AO, the SOPARFI circular LIR 14/4, the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, and the OECD 'substance over form' standards; a fitness-app SARL must demonstrate, where treaty or EU tax advantages are claimed, a local decision-making seat, actual employees and payroll, an operational fixed establishment, real administrative management in Luxembourg, and economic ownership of the developed software; the mere centralisation of sales revenue through a Luxembourg mailbox without local development, management or risk absorption enables recharacterisation of the Luxembourg entity as a conduit, denial of tax residence benefits, and reallocation of the entire commercial profit to the foreign beneficial owner's jurisdiction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underdeclaring Apple IAP and Google Play Billing net proceeds, destroying transaction records, issuing false invoices for apparent app-store commissions, or concealing the ultimate beneficial ownership of the SARL in a non-cooperative tax haven
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of one to five years under §§396-397 AO; automatic addition of the evaded tax and interest at 0.8% per month; extended 10-year assessment period for tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director or any signatory of the false return is jointly and severally liable for the evaded taxes, penalties and interest; criminal conviction may trigger a travel ban, asset freeze, publication of the sanction, and disqualification from managing any Luxembourg commercial company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling the developed app source code to a zero-tax related entity at book value while continuing to manage, update and commercialise the product; paying inflated management fees to the foreign parent; absence of written transfer-pricing policy for the 15-30% app-store commissions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment by Luxembourg tax administration, recharacterisation of the transactions under the arm's length principle, additional CIT assessed at 24.94%, late-payment interest, and an increase of up to 10% on the tax deficit; DAC6 disclosure violations carry separate fines of EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany agreements without economic justification incur civil liability for restitution of the corporate loss; in bankruptcy, the 'action en comblement du passif' allows the liquidator to recover the unreported commercial value from the directors' personal assets; aggravating circumstances lead to criminal sanctions for fraudulent impoverishment of the company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity with no employees in Luxembourg, no physical office except the registered address, board meetings held exclusively abroad, and all critical commercial decisions (app pricing, marketing, financing, IP management) taken by a foreign parent without local involvement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the claimed Luxembourg residence for tax treaty purposes, reallocation of all business profits to the beneficial owner's state, loss of the participation exemption and IP-box regime, additional tax assessments, penalties, and potential application of the EU anti-tax-avoidance directives; the Luxembourg tax administration may impose fines under the general tax law for failure to keep local books and records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly maintaining the shell structure are personally liable for the additional corporate taxes and penalties; a travel ban and seizure of personal assets can be ordered during the tax fraud investigation; European investment and pension fund victims of the conduit structure may bring civil claims against the nominee directors and managers

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Distribution and Shareholder Loan Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends exceeding the distributable reserves certified in the audited annual accounts, or disguising profit extraction as 'interest' or 'royalties' without a valid written loan or licence agreement, particularly where the Luxembourg SARL lacks the capacity to pay
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the purported interest or royalty payments as dividends subject to 15% WHT, or outright denial of the deduction; penalty interest of 0.8% per month; company law invalidation of the unlawful distribution; criminal fines for fraudulent distribution under the Law of 10 August 1915
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 710-18 of the Luxembourg Companies Law, directors must restore to the company any sums improperly distributed; in insolvency, creditors may initiate an 'action en comblement du passif' against the managers; fraudulent distribution in the face of insolvency is punishable by imprisonment up to five years and personal asset seizure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and register the ultimate beneficial owner of the SARL with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within 30 days of incorporation, or knowingly supplying inaccurate ownership data for the fitness-app commercial profits and dividend beneficiaries
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000 per violation and criminal fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons in aggravated cases; imprisonment of up to six months for individuals who fail to disclose UBO information after formal notice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The appointed manager or the statutory officer responsible for the UBO filing is personally prosecuted; where the hidden beneficial owner is using the SARL for money laundering of app-generated revenue, directors without an adequate AML governance framework face confiscation orders and civil damages for third-party losses

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Use of Treaty and EU Directives (GAAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating artificial holding structures where the sole purpose is to channel the digital health app's dividend flows through Luxembourg to obtain the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive rate or a third-state treaty benefit, without legitimate business purpose or genuine shareholding substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule and the EU anti-abuse jurisprudence (Danish Cases C-116/16 and C-117/16); denial of the WHT exemption and imposition of 15% WHT on the full dividend flow; additional tax interest, fines and publicity of the abusive arrangement; DAC6 mandatory exchange of information on the scheme with penalties for non-disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and the Luxembourg tax representative who signed the treaty relief forms may be jointly liable for the unpaid WHT if they knew or should have known of the artificiality; professional intermediaries (banks, auditors, tax advisers) are also subject to fines up to EUR 250,000 and potential imprisonment for complicity in tax evasion
